newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMutual more confident on China licence.
newsitem.headline: NatMutual more confident on China licence.

text.p: National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it was more confident about obtaining a licence to operate in China following the recent visit to China by Australian prime minister John Howard.

"We are more positive about our chances of securing a licence in China as a result of the visit of the prime minister," Tomlinson told reporters after an address to a luncheon hosted by the Committee for the Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).
However, Tomlinson said this did not not mean company expected to obtain a licence.

"The business community who participated in that three or four day sojourn in Beijing and Shanghai greatly appreciated the way we were treated and the way that the prime minister attempted to push our commercial interests of all of us and I think we are now seeing some benefits come through," he said.
The decision by Chinese vice premier Zhu Rongji to come to Australia later this month was an indication of the success of the Howard visit, Tomlinson said.
"In terms of relationships, trade and business opportunities in China, it must be seen as a very positive step and something that couldn't have been contemplated 12 months ago," Tomlinson said.
Howard visited China at the start of April and met Chinese president Jiang Zemin in an attempt to bolster economic ties between the two countries.
China is Australia's fifth largest trading partner, with two-way trade worth A$6.3 billion in the year to June 30, 1996.
